title: Interactive quickstart: side-by-side code & request-builder screenshots
creator: Ava Patel
description: Design and deliver a set of high-fidelity screenshots and annotated assets for the Hosted API getting-started experience. The focus is an interactive two-pane flow that pairs a visual request-builder with live code snippets (curl + Node/JS SDK) and an inline model quick-compare widget. These assets will be used in docs, the console tour, and release notes.
goals: Provide clear, copy-ready screenshots for docs that show model selection, preset prompts, and token estimates
Demonstrate side-by-side request builder and synchronized code snippets (curl + JS) in a single frame
Surface model quick-compare micro-pane (latency/cost/quality) without overwhelming the main UI
Create assets that work at both hero-size (1200x700) and narrow doc widths (760x420)
acceptance_criteria: Exported PNG and SVG screenshots for three variations: (1) model picker open, (2) request builder with preset selected, (3) request builder with streaming response in progress
Each screenshot includes an accessible alt text candidate and short caption strings for docs
Figma frames annotated with callouts for microcopy and code placeholders (api_key, model id)
Design reviewed and signed off by PM (Maya Chen) and Eng lead (Ravi Singh)
PRD link and final image files uploaded to Drive and linked in ticket
assets: Figma file: Hosted API / Quickstart / Interactive-code-walkthrough (page: Screenshots)
design tokens: color & spacing spec (figma page)
steps: Finalize UI treatment in Figma: flex layout with left request builder, right code pane, top model quick-compare chip
Create three content states: model selection, preset request populated, streaming response with token meter anim-state
Generate hero PNG (1200x700) with PR-ready labels and caption
Export narrow PNG (760x420) suitable for docs sidebar
Write alt text and 1-line caption for each image and add to Drive annotations doc
Upload assets to Drive and attach to this ticket; leave a link in comments
Request sign-off from PM and Eng; incorporate feedback; finalize
design_notes: Use monospaced font for code pane; show both curl and Node snippet toggles
Token-estimate meter uses three bands (cheap/medium/expensive) and shows tooltip on hover
Model quick-compare should show 3 micro-metrics: median latency, cost/1k tokens, and short-quality tag (e.g., 'good for chat')
Avoid showing real API keys — use placeholder '<API_KEY>' and a redacted badge
Ensure contrast for accessibility (WCAG AA) for code text and interactive chips
decisions: Primary hero will use a light background with subtle card shadows to match docs aesthetic
Streaming state will show partial text with a blue pulse to indicate live tokens rather than animated GIFs
We will include both curl and Node snippets simultaneously in hero to reduce cognitive load for engineers
Model quick-compare will be collapsed by default in narrow view, expanded in hero-size
